chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said:
For one who is fearful, there is no harm in stoning the Jamarat at night, slaughtering the sacrifice at night, and proceeding at night.

key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the Jamarat, the ritual stoning sites in hajj
key_terms.الْخَائِفِ: the person who is fearful or apprehensive of harm
key_terms.يَرْمِيَ: to throw, here meaning to cast pebbles at the Jamarat
key_terms.يُفِيضَ: to proceed or depart, here referring to ifadah during hajj

ai.seo_question: Is a fearful pilgrim allowed to stone the Jamarat and perform other hajj rites at night?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal concession for a person who fears harm during the rites of hajj. It permits such a person to perform the stoning of the Jamarat, the sacrifice, and the departure or ifadah at night.
